text:
incident-bot: P1 detected — elevated 95th latency on /v1/generate (hosted inference-api, west1). Automated threshold hit at 17:10 UTC, paging @oncall. metrics: 95th=1.2s (baseline 350ms), p50~120ms, errors 5xx ~2%.
Aisha Patel: I'm catching this. On-call here — spinning up bridge in #incidents. Ben, you available to drive? I need someone to own comms too.
Ben Gomez: I can drive for the next 30–45m. Will pull logs and check autoscaler. Taking primary.
Carla Ng: I can take comms for now. I'll start a short status post for customers and update the incident doc.
Dan O'Neill: Noted. I'll act as secondary (infra). If it looks like GPU pool saturation, I'll check Dedicated fallback routing.
Aisha Patel: quick notes: suspected source is batching/backpressure from a new client rollout hitting long sequences. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/runbooks/inference-latency (see section "sequence length surge").
Ben Gomez: running quick checks: 
```
# tail recent error spikes
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-api --since=15m | grep "timeout\|oom\|KVcache"
# inspect queue depth
redis-cli -h cache-west1 LRANGE inflight 0 50
```
Ben Gomez: seeing increased queue depth and a few timed out calls in runtime logs. KV cache hits down ~10%. autoscaler shows pod CPU fine but GPU utilization hitting 90% on a subset of nodes.
Carla Ng: posting initial customer-facing note: "We're investigating increased latency for some hosted generation requests in west1. Some requests may be slower than usual. We're triaging — will update in 15m." Posting now. :rotating_light:
Aisha Patel: mitigation options — (1) route new traffic to smaller model variant (fast-legacy) via routing policy, (2) enable aggressive batching throttle, (3) scale up ephemeral GPU pool (if quota allows), (4) rollback client's rollout if possible. Ben, what's fastest?
Ben Gomez: fastest is route high-seq clients to fast-legacy and enable prefix KV cache warming. I'll open a canary routing change: `rb route set --target fast-legacy --filter 'client:abc123' --ttl 1800` and trigger cache-warming job. If that doesn't drop p95 in 5–10m, request +2 nodes.
Eve Zhuang: FYI I can run the cache-warm job and monitor downstream e2e latencies post-change.
Dan O'Neill: if we add nodes, prefer west1b to spread load. I've verified capacity available +2 GPUs there.
Carla Ng: updated customers: added that we're routing heavy clients to a faster variant while we stabilize. Will schedule a follow-up update at 17:30 UTC.
Ben Gomez: made routing change at 17:16 UTC (audit id r-9a8f). Observing metrics... p95 dropping from 1.2s -> 780ms after 2m. Good sign.
Aisha Patel: assign ownership for the handoff: Ben - incident driver (primary) until 18:00 UTC, Carla - comms owner (customer updates, post-incident summary), Eve - secondary ops for cache/monitoring tasks, Dan - infra escalation/scale ops. I'll remain in bridge until handoff at 17:50.
Carla Ng: noted. I'll draft a postmortem template with timeline and customer impact: affected requests ~2% of requests in west1 during window, errors 5xx spike to 2.1%, no data loss.
Ben Gomez: p95 stable ~420–500ms now after routing + cache warm; leaving autoscaler scale request pending for +2 nodes as backup.
Aisha Patel: coverage gap check — next on-call arrives at 17:55 UTC (shift change). Ben, please ensure runbook steps and the routing rollback command are in the incident doc so incoming can resume quickly. Carla, add comms handoff note for next shift.
Ben Gomez: adding the exact rollback snippet to incident doc now: `rb route rollback r-9a8f` and `kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-api --to-revision=23` if needed.
Eve Zhuang: I'll keep the dashboard alert on for another 30m and make a short playbook note about sequence-length detection threshold.
Carla Ng: handoff checklist posted in thread: 1) driver update + metrics, 2) commands run + audit ids, 3) comms draft + scheduled update, 4) infra scale status, 5) next shift contact info.
Aisha Patel: final for now — driver=Ben, comms=Carla, secondary=Eve, infra escalation=Dan. Next shift (17:55) ping @oncall for takeover. If anything regresses, revert routing and call for full P0.
Ben Gomez: acknowledged. I'll be around until 18:10 in case follow-up needed.
Carla Ng: thanks all — I'll push final customer update at 17:30 and add incident notes for the incoming shift. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status summary updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring, severity=P1 -> P1 (no escalation). Audit: r-9a8f, actions=[route-change, cache-warm].
